summary: Authorization request: ephemeral customer-session metadata export + reversible ID mapping for triage of deduplication regression
description:
Issue summary:
Request from SRE (bug triage) to produce a minimal exported table of session-level metadata paired with a reversible mapping to internal customer IDs for debugging a near-real-time deduplication regression affecting production traffic.

Impact:
- Tooling team needs to link anonymized session fingerprints back to customer accounts to reproduce and fix dedup logic that is incorrectly merging sessions.
- No raw prompt/response text requested. Request is limited to metadata fields.
- Potential privacy risk if reversible mapping is retained beyond troubleshooting window.

Requested export fields (proposed minimal set):
- session_fingerprint (hash of first-32-bytes of kv prefix, salted)
- session_start_ts (UTC)
- session_end_ts (UTC)
- route/model/version (e.g., redwood-medium-13b, v2026-01-15)
- peak_token_rate (tokens/sec)
- request_count
- error_count
- customer_id_mapping_key (ephemeral token that can be reversed to customer_id by Security only)

Retention & access constraints proposed:
- Mapping reversible only via Security runbook (HSM-backed unwrap) and only for explicit SRE triage tickets.
- Export TTL: 72 hours. After TTL, both export and mapping key to be destroyed and audit recorded.
- Access ACL: SRE triage group + Security approver; no external contractor access.
- Export stored encrypted (KMS) and accessible only via temporary signed URL with MFA.

Environment:
- Production, us-east-1. Narrow time window requested: 2026-01-25 08:00 to 2026-01-25 12:00 UTC (approximate window where regression spike observed).

Steps to reproduce (SRE notes):
1) Observe dedup regression spike on 2026-01-25 08:30 UTC on route /v1/chat/stream.
2) Attempt to trace by session fingerprint correlation; without mapping to customer accounts engineers cannot reproduce account-specific routing configuration that triggers failure.

Logs & references:
- SLO dashboard: https://observability.redwood/dashboard/dedup-regression-2026-01-25
- Incident stub: INC-55912 (investigation ongoing)
- Slack thread: #sre-debug (https://slack.redwood/archives/C12345)

Proposed mitigations requested with authorization:
- Security review and sign-off for ephemeral mapping (72h)
- Runbook step to perform mapping unwrap with two-person approval (Security + Eng lead)
- Automated purge job scheduled immediately after TTL with audit event written to audit-logs-prod

Approval needed from: Security (data-access), Privacy, SRE lead, and Legal approval for cross-customer mapping in production.
investigation_notes: SRE collected aggregated metrics and confirmed anomaly window; no PII currently accessible in exported metadata set.
Initial attempt to reproduce using synthetic accounts did not surface dedup condition; hypothesis is customer-specific config or routing policy.
Checked serving-runtime logs for model rollouts around time window; one canary variant was active on ~2026-01-25 08:20 UTC (see infra PR 4102).
Risk assessment: reversible mapping is sensitive; recommend HSM unwrap and two-person approval. Potential legal concern if mapping is retained longer than agreed TTL.
comments: Asha Patel (reporter) - 2026-01-28: Filing this to get rapid authorization. SRE cannot proceed without ability to tie fingerprints to customer accounts. No content payload requested.

Miguel Rivera (SRE) - 2026-01-29: Confirmed dedup spike in us-east at 08:30 UTC. I propose limiting export to the 4-hour window and using one-way salted hashes for fingerprints; still need mapping for final step.

Priya Menon (Security) - 2026-01-30: Security OK in principle if mapping unwrap uses HSM and two-person approval. Need Legal sign-off for reversible mapping even if short-lived. Please attach proposed access list and retention automation plan.

Legal (Emma Dawson) - 2026-02-01: Reviewed. We will approve ephemeral mapping for 72 hours for triage only. Require signed attestation from Eng lead and Security. Add audit event and retention proof in Confluence runbook.

Samir Gupta (assignee) - 2026-02-03: I will coordinate Security approval steps and create the ephemeral export job with KMS encryption and automated purge. Blocking: final sign-off from Eng lead (Jordan Lee).
resolution_notes: Pending: Security + Eng lead sign-off received? (Partial). Legal approved ephemeral 72-hour mapping with attestation. Final action: Samir to run export and record audit events; then purge after TTL.
